albums.blurb: Joe Pass spent the 1950s and 60s as a working sideman before Norman Granz signed him to the new Pablo label and, in a single August 1973 session in Los Angeles, recorded him completely alone. Virtuoso is the result: standards like "Night and Day" and "Cherokee" played with walking bass, chords and melody carried simultaneously on one unaccompanied guitar, a format almost nobody had built a whole record on before. It launched a four-volume Virtuoso series and a decade of Pablo work alongside Ella Fitzgerald and Oscar Peterson.
albums.reception: Both AllMusic and The Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide rate it five stars, The Penguin Guide to Jazz Recordings places it in its core collection, and it reached No. 16 on Billboard's jazz albums chart in 1974.

albums.blurb: Older is the Philadelphia songwriter's third album and her first for RCA, following 2022's five seconds flat, whose slow-burn hit "ceilings" made her a streaming breakout. Where that record leaned on pop production, Older strips back to piano, acoustic guitar and close-miked vocals across fourteen short songs about a relationship's slow end; a deluxe edition, Older (and Wiser), followed in late 2024 with five additional tracks.
albums.reception: The album debuted at No. 93 on the Billboard 200 and also charted in Australia, Ireland and New Zealand, with critics' reviews noting her artistic growth and maturity, and its singles "Older" and "I Guess" reached Nos. 33 and 26 on Billboard's Hot Rock & Alternative Songs chart.

albums.blurb: Broadcast were a Birmingham group built around singer Trish Keenan and bassist James Cargill, who filtered 1960s psychedelic pop — above all the short-lived American band The United States of America — through analogue synthesizers and library-music atmospheres. The Noise Made by People, released on Warp in March 2000 after the Work and Non Work singles compilation, is their debut studio album, self-recorded and self-produced after sessions with outside engineers left them dissatisfied. Keenan died in 2011, and the band's small catalogue has only grown in stature since.
albums.reception: The album peaked at No. 79 on the UK Albums Chart, and Pitchfork's contemporary review scored it 7.8, praising the sound while finding the band's vision narrow.
